question: Should a woman who took her husband's last name change it back to her father's name?
asked: I got married about 20 years ago and took my husband's last name. Now I am being told that this goes against the Qur'an. Should I legally change my name back to what it was before I got married?
answer:
This is a simple response. Allah says in the Qur'an, "Call them by their fathers; that is the justice in the eyes of Allah." And this verse has been misinterpreted by some in our modern times to say that it applies to women changing their last names. But this is not the case.

The Western concept of a woman changing her last name (and this is coming from the West; it never existed in the East) is a complete European construct, where if a lady would marry a man, she would change her last name to indicate that she is now basically owned by the man, or she belongs to the man. Even in Western culture, it was never meant to indicate that she is no longer the daughter of her own father. You see, the Western function of the last name is not the same as the Qur'anic verse. The Qur'anic verse, "Call them by their fathers," means make sure that the child is said to be so-and-so the son of so-and-so, so-and-so the daughter of so-and-so, and do not substitute the son or daughter of so-and-so with another name that is not the parent.

Now, in our modern culture, the first name is our name. The family name keeps on changing every few generations; this is the default. Hardly any family maintains its name for a lengthy period of time. And there are some family names that are so common, you have millions and billions of people that might have the exact same family name, which means nothing then. The family name in and of itself is not an identity marker of "call them by their fathers"; that doesn't apply there.

Does this mean she should change her name when she gets married? No. Why should she not change her name? Because it is a notion of ownership that Europe had, and there's no need to do this. **So if a lady marries, she should not change her last name, Islamically speaking.**

If it has happened in the past and she has already changed all of her legal documents to her husband's name, she is not obliged to go back and redo the whole process. It is permissible to let it be. She is not contradicting the verse in the Qur'an, because it is not ascribing her to other than her father. However, in her informal introductions, in her talks and whatnot, other than her passport, she should go back to the name of her family, because we do not agree, Islamically speaking, that the wife belongs to the husband the way that Europe did. And there is no need to change the last name: even if it is not an identity marker of the parents, it is still an identity marker of the family, and she does belong to that family that she was born into.

So, bottom line: if the lady is about to get married, she should not change the last name. If the last name has legally been changed and now she wants to change it, she may do so informally; she should do so informally. But she is not obliged to go to a court of law. If she wants to, she may; I'm not saying she shouldn't. But she's not sinful, is what I'm trying to say. And Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala knows best.
